title: The たら and なら conditionals
summary: たら is the past form plus ら: "once that has happened". It alone can talk about the past. なら attaches to a noun or clause as "if it is the case that".

blocks.text: Conditionals often swap places, but each has its own flavor. Here are the last two.
たら: the past form + ら
Take any verb or adjective in its **past** form (た / だ / かった) and add **ら**. It means "once that is done". Because it builds on the past, it fits situations that are already fulfilled.

blocks.jp: 起きたら、雪が積もっていた。
blocks.en: When I got up, snow had piled up.

blocks.jp: 家に帰ったら、さくらがいた。
blocks.en: When I got home, Sakura was there.

blocks.text: In the past, たら is the only conditional you can use, and it means **"when"** and often carries **surprise**: plain て or から would be flat; an if-word says "I did not expect this".
For the future, たら stresses **what happens once the condition is met**, while ば stresses **whether it will be met at all**. When you expect the condition to happen, たら leans towards "when".

blocks.jp: 雨がやんだら、出かけよう。
blocks.en: Once the rain stops, let's go out.

blocks.text: A small っ gives **ったら** (and the stronger **ってば**): a shortened "when it comes to ..." with a tone of mild complaint, often teasing.

blocks.jp: お母さんったら、また忘れたの。

blocks.text: **なら** attaches directly to a noun or a full clause. It takes up what was said or is clearly the case: "if it's X (as you say / as it is)".

blocks.en: If it's Sakura, she can do it.
If you mean the station, it is over there.

items: **Past form + ら**: once that has happened; the only if-form for the past.
In the past, it can carry surprise.
**Noun or clause + なら**: if it is the case that; "since it's X".

questions.instruction: Pick the たら form of 飲む
Pick the たら form of 寒い
Pick the たら form of 静かだ
questions.note: Past 静かだった + ら.

questions.prompt: 窓を開けたら、猫が入ってきた。
options: If I open it, a cat will come in
When I opened it, a cat (surprisingly) came in
I wish a cat would come in
questions.note: In the past, たら means "when" and implies surprise.
questions.en: When I opened the window, a cat came in.

questions.prompt: ドアを開けたら、誰もいなかった。
questions.note: たら in the past: an unexpected result.
questions.en: When I opened the door, nobody was there.

questions.prompt: 仕事が終わったら、電話してください。
options: Please call me once work is over
questions.note: たら: once that has happened.
questions.en: Please call me once work is over.

questions.prompt: あした天気がよかっ＿＿、公園に行こう。
questions.en: If the weather is good tomorrow, let's go to the park.

questions.instruction: What does なら do in B's answer?
questions.prompt: A「来週、名古屋に行くんです。」B「名古屋なら、おてらがおすすめですよ。」
options: Picks up the topic just raised
questions.note: なら: given that it's X.
questions.en: A: I'm going to Nagoya next week. B: If it's Nagoya, I recommend the temples.

questions.prompt: A「日本語の辞書がほしいです。」B「辞書なら、私のを貸しますよ。」
options: If it's a dictionary, I'll lend you mine
questions.note: なら attaches to a noun just mentioned.
questions.en: A: I want a Japanese dictionary. B: If it's a dictionary, I'll lend you mine.

questions.prompt: コンビニ＿＿、あそこにありますよ。
questions.note: なら picks up what was asked about.
questions.en: If you mean a convenience store, there is one over there.

questions.prompt: さくらが行く＿＿、私も行く。
questions.note: Clause + なら: if it is the case that.
questions.en: If Sakura goes, I'll go too.

questions.prompt: お父さんったら、また寝ているの。

questions.instruction: In which sentence has it already happened, with a feeling of surprise?
options: 雨が降ったら、休みます。
家に帰ったら、手紙が来ていた。
暇だったら、来てください。
questions.note: Past result after たら: a surprise.

questions.prompt: たら is built from the past form plus ら.

options: 暑かったら、窓を開けます。
雨だったら、行きません。
静かだったら、読めます。
questions.note: A noun or な-word needs だった before ら.

questions.prompt: If those shoes are cheap, I will buy them.
questions.en: If those shoes are cheap, I will buy them.

questions.prompt: When I opened my bag, my wallet was not there.
questions.en: When I opened my bag, my wallet was not there.

questions.prompt: If it's Nagoya, it's two hours by train.
questions.en: If it's Nagoya, it's two hours by train.

questions.prompt: Once school is over, let's eat.
questions.en: Once school is over, let's eat.
Contact me when you arrive home.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that picks up the topic that was raised
questions.en: If it's a trip, Hokkaido is good.
